text:
kevin: quick question about the new "Service overview" chart in Figma — we show throughput (req/s) + p95 latency (ms) over time in one view. should we use dual y axes or keep a single normalized scale?
anya: avoid dual axes unless it's impossible. folks misread them all the time.
sam: agree. space is tight though. options: stacked mini-rows, normalized percent-of-baseline, or keep single axis and show absolute values on hover/tooltips.
jules: Accessibility: hover-dependent info is not enough. screen readers need a text summary that includes both units. propose hidden paragraph: "Throughput in requests per second and 95th percentile latency in milliseconds are shown. Use point hover or the data table for absolute values."
kevin: +1. UX for visual clarity: large ms spikes blow out the scale. options: cap visuals at 99th percentile, flag capped points as outliers, or allow a toggle "show raw extremes".
anya: capping + marker is my vote. add a dashed cap line and greyed-out outlier dots. put a small info icon on the axis: "Some extreme values capped for visualization."
sam: note for smoothing: compute smoothing on raw series (e.g., rolling median) then render the smoothed line over the capped raw series so trends don't disappear.
jules: legend: add per-series unit chips like "· req/s" and "· ms" visually, but for SR read full words: "Throughput, requests per second" etc.
kevin: short formatter rules idea:
```
if (unit === 'req/s') tick = siShort(value)
if (unit === 'ms') tick = Math.round(value) + ' ms'
```
anya: also ensure export PNG respects capping note in the axis tooltip and include a metadata field in the CSV export: "outlier_policy: capped at 99th pct by default".
sam: ownership: @anya update Figma with stacked-mini and capped-marker variant; @jules will draft the SR paragraph and aria-live example; I'll add the smoothing implementation note to the tickets.
design-bot: summary: "Prefer capping at 99th pct with outlier markers; avoid dual axis; provide unit chips in legend + SR-friendly descriptions; smoothing computed on raw data then rendered on capped visuals; expose toggle to show raw extremes."
kevin: thanks all, will iterate on the mock and follow up.
